c.p: Which of these is the main reason why day length and weather change throughout the year?
c.a: The Earth orbits the Sun on a tilted axis
c.h: Think about how our planet moves around the Sun and its tilt.
c.e: Earth experiences four distinct seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter) because of its orbit and tilt, causing changes in weather and day length.
r: Common misconception: Many believe Earth is closer to the Sun in summer, but seasons are caused by the Earth's tilted axis as it orbits.
Weather changes between seasons, but clouds are not the cause of astronomical seasons.

c.p: In the UK, during which season do we experience the shortest daylight hours and coldest temperatures?
c.h: Think about snow, short days, and cold weather.
c.e: In Winter, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun, resulting in shorter daylight hours and lower temperatures.
r: Autumn precedes winter as days get shorter, but the shortest days occur in winter.
Spring brings longer days and warming temperatures after winter.

c.p: What noticeable change happens to deciduous trees during Autumn in the UK?
c.a: Their leaves change colour and fall off
c.h: Think about walking through leaves in the park in October.
c.e: Deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn to conserve water and survive the cold winter months.
r: New shoots and buds typically appear in Spring.
Summer fruits develop in warm summer months.

c.p: What seasonal pattern begins when flowers start blooming, baby animals are born, and days get longer?
c.h: Think of daffodils and baby lambs.
c.e: Spring marks the transition from winter to summer with new plant growth and animal breeding as daylight increases.
r: Winter has the coldest temperatures and dormant plant life.
Summer follows spring with the longest and warmest days.
